claims: Issue #584 reports s(339) <= 18.926898900357, s(364) <= 19.583782203951 and s(375) <= 19.882451030482, the exact rational sides of the certificates rounded up at 12 places, for the beyond-horizon list; it prints the certificate sides 18.92689890035674158973360842897, 19.583782203950834292109305759091 and 19.882451030481246819527281665997 with the SHA-256 of each search/packer/candidates/comp2_nNNN.cert.

The issue says all three are two-piece compositions, a rectangle of unit squares whose sides differ by an integer in each of two opposite corners and aligned squares filling the rest: at 339 two pieces cut from Daniil Ostashev's s(304) of issue 575, at 364 BuddenPing's s(146) of issue 566 whole with Thomas Schadt's s(50) = 53/7, so S* = s(146) + 7, and at 375 a 69-square crop of Nate Chaoweeraprasit's (SQUISH) s(88) with a 118-square crop of Ryan Xu's s(129), so S* = s(88) + 10 to 13 digits.
Through Friedman's L-step the issue also states s(403) <= 20.583782203951 and s(414) <= 20.882451030482 as corollaries, for which it asks no rows.

Each side is an 80-digit KKT point with positive multipliers on the load-bearing contacts, a reduced Hessian positive semidefinite modulo exact flat motions and a first-order MILP that finds no descent; the issue calls these numerical evidence, not interval proofs, and claims no optimality.
